paragraphs.en: A reproduction of Botswana's famed Okavango Blue Diamond is just one of artist John Hatleberg's works.
paragraphs.zh: 博茨瓦纳著名的奥卡万戈蓝钻高仿品只是艺术家约翰·哈特伯格的作品之一。

paragraphs.en: This one displayed in New York City's Diamond District, but one especially precious to Hatleberg will be shown at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington D.C., a reproduction of the legendary Blue Diamond of the French Crown.
paragraphs.zh: 这件在纽约市钻石区展出，但哈特伯格特别珍爱的一件作品将在华盛顿特区的史密森研究院展出，即传奇的王冠蓝钻高仿品。

paragraphs.en: The artist says this is what the gem looked like until mid-19th century before it disappeared and later reemerged as the iconic Hope Diamond.
paragraphs.zh: 这位艺术家称，这就是这颗宝石在十九世纪中叶之前的模样，之后它便下落不明，后来又以标志性的“希望钻石”的身份重新出现在人们视野中。

paragraphs.en: So what I'm going to show you this diamond is one of the few conceptual gem cuts I've ever seen in my life, and it's really kind of astounding.
paragraphs.zh: 我要向你们展示的这颗钻石，是我这辈子见过的为数不多的概念性宝石切割作品之一，真的相当令人惊叹。

paragraphs.en: Louis XIV, known as the Sun King, his colors were blue and gold. He has this blue diamond and he wants this to really represent his power.
paragraphs.zh: 路易十四，人称太阳王，他的代表色是蓝色和金色。他拥有这颗蓝钻石，并且希望它能真正彰显自己的权力。

paragraphs.en: The stone's biography stretches through five centuries. In the 17th century a giant 115-carat stone was brought to France from India.
paragraphs.zh: 这块宝石的传奇跨越了五个世纪。17世纪，一颗115克拉的巨石从印度运到法国。

paragraphs.en: It was cut for Louis XIV when it became known as the Blue French Crown Diamond. Since then it's been recut many times to suit the taste of its new owners.
paragraphs.zh: 这颗钻石是为路易十四切割的，后来被称为王冠蓝钻。此后，它被多次重新切割，以迎合新主人的品味。

paragraphs.en: It would have taken years to recreate the famous stone, but employees of the Louver Museum in Paris happened to find two cast iron molds of the diamond ordered by Louis XIV himself.
paragraphs.zh: 复刻这颗著名的宝石本需要耗费数年时间，但巴黎卢浮宫的员工碰巧找到了两副由路易十四本人定制的钻石铸铁模具。

paragraphs.en: It can't be extremely brilliant because the light goes right through it. They made a sun, a seven-ray sun in the back of this, and they set it in gold.
paragraphs.zh: 它不可能极其璀璨，因为光线会直接穿透它。他们在它的背面制作了一个有七道光芒的太阳，并镶上黄金。

paragraphs.en: And because the light goes right through the center instead on the center essentially, it reflected that seven-ray gold sun, so there he was, Louis XIV, the Sun God with his blue diamond with the gold sun radiating out from it.
paragraphs.zh: 由于光线基本上是直穿中心而非在中心反射，它映照出那七道光芒的金色太阳，太阳王路易十四佩戴着他的蓝色钻石，金色的阳光从中向外辐射。

paragraphs.en: Hatleberg says getting the shape right was one challenge, but getting the color right was the toughest part.
paragraphs.zh: 哈特伯格说，做出合适的形状是一项挑战，但调出合适的颜色才是最困难的部分。

paragraphs.en: He got help from a Minnesota company that uses a technique of spattering nanoparticles.
paragraphs.zh: 他从明尼苏达州一家公司获得了帮助，该公司采用了一种喷射纳米粒子的技术。

paragraphs.en: If you take a thin sheet of a gold leaf and hold it up to a strong light, the color coming through it doesn't transmit. Gold color transmits blue.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你拿一片薄金箔对着强光看，透过来的颜色不是金色。金色透射出来的是蓝色。

paragraphs.en: The precious metal part of it is gold essentially. The nanodot we all know nanodots are now so just very small particles of gold and the physical vapor part, physical vapor just means cloud.
paragraphs.zh: 贵金属部分本质上就是黄金。我们都知道纳米点现在就是非常微小的金颗粒，而物理气相只是指云状物。

paragraphs.en: So you have this nanodot gold cloud that's deposited on the back of these replicas.
paragraphs.zh: 在这些高仿品的背面沉积着纳米点金云。

paragraphs.en: Hatleberg first used this technology in 2010 to replicate the Hope Diamond itself at the Smithsonian Institution.
paragraphs.zh: 哈特伯格在2010年首次使用这项技术在史密森研究院高仿了希望钻石。

paragraphs.en: Once the Smithsonian reopens after the coronavirus pandemic comes to an end, it will feature an earlier version of the Hope Diamond, a new starring gem called the Blue Diamond of the French Crown.
paragraphs.zh: 待新冠疫情结束后史密森研究院重新开放时，将展出希望钻石的一个更早版本，也就是一颗新晋成为焦点的宝石王冠蓝钻。
